summary: ASTRO NOVA is an astronaut health monitoring system designed to monitor and manage the physical well-being of astronauts during space missions. We developed a space-themed web application that provides real-time health monitoring, tracks vital parameters such as heart rate, body temperature, blood oxygen rate, and other health indicators, and displays the collected data through an interactive dashboard. The system aims to identify abnormal health conditions, generate alerts, and help astronauts and mission control respond quickly to medical emergencies as soon as possible. It addresses the challenges of limited medical facilities, communication delays, and health risks in space environments. The project combines React.js, TypeScript, Node.js, and modern technologies to create an accessible and user-friendly platform. Its key innovation is bringing multiple health-monitoring features into one centralized system, with the potential for offline functionality and future integration with wearable sensors. ASTRO NOVA aims to improve astronaut safety, enable early health-risk detection, and support safer, longer-duration space missions.
details: ASTRO NOVA is an astronaut health-monitoring platform designed to improve astronaut safety and healthcare during space missions. It helps astronauts monitor important health parameters such as heart rate, blood oxygen rate, body temperature, track sleep, report symptoms and it also contains an AI voice support system. The platform includes three dashboards: Astronaut, Medical Team and Admin, allowing astronauts to monitor their health, doctors to review astronaut health information and administrators to manage medical inventory and system activities. It also provides features such as a Bluetooth wearable sensor connectivity and an Emergency SOS interface. We developed the website using React.js, TypeScript, HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Web Bluetooth APIs for connectivity to bluetooth devices, and we deployed it using Netlify. AI tools assisted us with code generation, design improvements and debugging. The project aims to support early identification of potential health risks, improve medical coordination and make healthcare more accessible during space missions. Its creative approach combines multiple healthcare features into one astronaut-focused platform. During development, we considered astronaut safety, ease of use, sensor accuracy, data security, connectivity, reliability and future offline functionality. Our future goal is to integrate real wearable sensors, improve offline capabilities and make ASTRO NOVA more reliable for long-duration space missions.
